name: News
description: Keeps each person's own News choices, private to the owner. People can pick catalog sources and topics, exclude publishers by domain, and remove sources they added. A person's added sources, topics and exclusions can be exported, and account deletion covers all nine News tables. A person can add a source by typing a site address or a subreddit. Moss reads the public site, finds its feed, asks the person's own AI model whether the source is acceptable, and shows a preview to confirm. Adding a topic or changing one needs web search, which is not part of this package, so those requests are refused. The News page is compiled from the active sources: stories are filtered, ranked by the person's own AI model with a fixed-order fallback, stored as a snapshot and served by the overview route. Changes to a person's choices queue a refresh job that rebuilds the page, and a daily check at 04:43 UTC re-reads every added source and topic and records its health. Story pictures and publisher icons are served only for stories and publishers the person already sees. Five chat tools read the stored headlines, check a source before it is added, report added-source status and ask for a refresh, and the Briefings module can read the top headlines. A person can mark a story as more or less like this; a story marked less is left out of the page, the chat tools, briefings and its picture. The News settings screen ships with this package.

news.heartbeatHeadlines.description: Read the top stories already stored for the signed-in person. Never contacts a news source. Takes only horizonHours (1 to 48) and limit (1 to 20).

news.topHeadlinesToday.description: Read today's top stories for the signed-in person as short lines plus the evidence each came from.

news.credentialedSourceStatus.description: List the sources the person added with their health and whether a key is saved, with a plain next step. Never shows a key.

news.previewSource.description: Check a publisher address or name and return candidates to confirm. Saves nothing and never shows a feed address.

news.refreshNews.description: Ask Moss to rebuild the person's news page. The work runs in the background.

settings.label: News
settings.description: Chosen sources and topics, excluded publishers and added sources can be changed through the News routes. The News settings screen shows built-in sources, added sources, topics, excluded publishers and story preferences.

features.description: Each person keeps a private list of chosen catalog sources and topics, and of publishers to leave out. Saving the same choice twice returns the first one. At most 100 publishers can be excluded.

errors.description: The person already excludes 100 publishers, so another cannot be added.

remediations.description: Remove a publisher from the excluded list, then add the new one.

features.description: A person can add a source by typing a site address or a subreddit name, and remove a source they added. Moss reads the public page over https, looks for its feed, and shows the result for the person to confirm. A site that is redirected to another publisher is refused, a source the person's AI model does not approve is refused, and a person can keep ten added sources. A source name with no address needs web search, which is not part of this package. Saving a source queues a refresh of the page.

errors.description: The site could not be checked right now, or the AI model gave no usable answer.

features.description: A person can remove a topic they added. Adding a topic or changing one needs web search, which is not part of this package, so those requests answer that discovery is unavailable.

errors.description: Topic discovery needs web search, which is not available in this package.

remediations.description: Remove the topic you no longer want. Adding topics returns with web search.

features.description: The News page is built from the catalog sources the person has on and the sources they added. Stories from excluded publishers, stories that are too old or repeats are left out. The person's own AI model ranks what is left, and when the model cannot answer the stories keep a fixed order by source and time. The built page is stored for seven days and the overview route serves it, queueing a background refresh when the stored page is missing or out of date. The refresh job rebuilds the page and keeps the last good page if every source fails. Any change to the person's sources, topics, chosen sources or excluded publishers queues a refresh too, and a person can ask for one directly.

A person can mark a story on their own page as more or less like this, with an optional reason of up to 500 characters, change the reason, and undo the choice. A story marked less is left out of the page, the chat tools and the briefing on every read, until the choice is undone. Choices are private to the person and hold only a story reference, never the headline or link. Story choices do not yet change how stories are ranked, and they are not shared with Briefings, Chat or Settings.

errors.description: The story is not on the person's page and has no earlier choice.

features.description: A story's picture and a publisher's icon are loaded by Moss on the person's behalf, so the person's browser never contacts the publisher. A picture is fetched only for a story in the person's own stored page, and an icon only for a catalog publisher or a source the person added. Pictures must be jpeg, png, gif or webp, and icons ico, png, gif or webp, checked by their first bytes. Pictures larger than about 700 KB are refused (the old limit was 2 MB) and icons larger than 256 KB are refused. The browser may keep a picture for five minutes and an icon for a day.

errors.description: The publisher's picture could not be read, was too large, or was not a picture.

features.description: Five chat tools. Reading the top stories, source status and checking a source need no approval. Asking for a refresh shows an approval card for Your news feed, built from the stored record. Story feedback is not part of this package yet, so stories carry no feedback reference.

Briefings reads up to five top stories from the stored page, with the source and a short summary for each. Nothing is fetched while a briefing is built. Without a stored page the briefing shows a news gap.

Once a day at 04:43 UTC, for each person who has added a source or topic, Moss re-reads every added source, asks the person's AI model again when the earlier approval is old, and records whether each source is healthy, unreachable or signed out. A source that could not be read is marked temporarily unavailable and is read again on the next check so it can recover. When a source or topic newly needs attention, one notification says so, with no names in it. A person can also start the check directly.

remediations.description: Open News settings to retry or remove the sources that need attention.
